The empty seeded-following check is armed by an 8-row plain draw (320/322).\n3. Echoed literal \u2014 no. Expected pages are hand-written literals. `_pages` only shapes them into (status, labels, cursor-flag) and does not perform production's ordering or cursor logic. The production code that turns each red is in the phase being built. Deleting the following read's ORDER BY (published_at, video_id, instance_domain) DESC turns 215 red. Deleting the 3-key strict cursor predicate turns 215 red (TA skipped or TB repeated) and 230 red. Deleting the CREATE INDEX statements in ensure_video_indexes and in the sync schema turns 357 and 369 red.\n4. One value \u2014 no. The order and cursor are read at six inputs: main, nsfw=1, limit 9, 524 sources, 1000 sources, and moderated vs unmoderated. Index keys are read on two creation paths, each run twice. Line 253 pins the moderated cursor to the unmoderated one, but 249/251 first require both page-1 cursors to be non-empty, and the strict-after page 2 is asserted separately. So it does not stand alone against a sibling.\n5. The double \u2014 no. Only the socket transport is replaced: the Handler subclass overrides __init__ to set rfile/wfile/headers, plus send_response, send_header and end_headers. The `server` is a SimpleNamespace data holder: a real sqlite connection, locks and config ints. No server method is stood in for. This is the same pattern tests/active/test_internal_client_reads.py:83 and test_search.py:68 use. Dispatch, body parsing, the read and _respond_rows are the Engine's own. The HTTP-level claims run against the real session Engine.\n6. It collects \u2014 yes, it collects. The collect-only output's raw pytest text (tests/last_test_output.txt) reads `18 tests collected`, and the file defines 14 functions, two of them parametrized (4 follows cases, 3 cursor cases): 5+1+4+1+3+1+1+2 = 18. The runner summary line said \"no tests\" only because it was a collect-only run. In the full run all 18 executed.\n7. Observed, not predicted. The page literals were observed: probe_54_phase1_literals.py, rerun this turn, ran the plan's draft read over this exact `_catalogue` and printed main, nsfw, exact, mod-open, mod-blocked and batched walks identical to MAIN_PAGES, NSFW_PAGES and the literals at 230/249/251. It also printed the wrong first-batch-only walk. The index expectations were observed too: probe_54_phase1_helpers.py printed `hand-made right == EXPECTED True` and an ASC variant reading False, plus today's (None, []) on both paths. Session-Engine behaviour was observed through probe_54_phase1_engine.py: mode=random seed {'random': True} with 4 rows and no cursor key; seeded+mode=following returns the same upnext seed and rows; mode=following answers 400 Unknown mode today. What could not be observed before the phase exists: the three error strings ('Invalid follows payload', 'Too many follow sources in request body', 'Invalid cursor') and the empty page's seed shape are the plan's specified contract, not a run's output. The implementing run's 200/400 bodies confirm them. No rewrite.\n8. Red, not green \u2014 yes, red. ValidateTests on the checkpoint: `[exit status 1]`, `17 failed, 1 passed`. The one green test is test_a_seeded_request_with_mode_following_and_follows_is_still_the_same_upnext. It guards a behaviour that already holds and must keep holding through the phase (the probe showed today's seeded+mode=following answer equals plain upnext). It carries no row.\n9. Red for the right reason \u2014 yes, every failure is on a judging assertion. All controls passed: _walk's returncode control at 185 passed (the walks returned bodies), the random-feed control at 280 passed (283 was reached), and the no-index control at 352 passed (357 was reached). The failures: line 215 failed on `([400], [\"answer: {'error': 'Unknown mode', 'allowed': ['recommendations', 'trending', 'recent', 'random', 'popular']}\"], False) != ([200], ['A3', 'X2', 'X1', 'TB'], True)`. Lines 221, 230, 241 and 249 failed on the same Unknown mode 400. Lines 283, 290, 297 and 304 failed with `{'error': 'Unknown mode', ...}`, e.g. 283 `assert (400, None) == (200, [])`. Line 310 failed on `(400, None, 0)`. Lines 357 and 369 failed on `{'idx_videos_channel_published': (None, [])} != {'idx_videos_channel_published': ('videos', [('instance_domain', 0), ('channel_id', 0), ('published_at', 1), ('video_id', 1)])}`. These failures show that mode=following and the recency indexes are not implemented. None is a typo, a missing import, a bad path or a harness defect.\n10. Observed expected output \u2014 every row's expected value matches what was run. The C1 rows' pages are the probe's printed walks of the draft read over the same catalogue, and this run contradicts none of them: it shows only today's 400, which the rows give as the current reading. The C2 rows' value is the probe's `hand-made right == EXPECTED True`, and this run's (None, []) is the wrong-implementation reading the rows name. No rewrite needed.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:1": "<changes>\nI made no production edits this turn. Every change the checkpoint needs was already in the working tree when I opened the files, apparently from an earlier pass of this step: an emptied probe of mine was still sitting at `tests/tmp/probe_following_phase1.py`. I read each file and traced the flow from the request edge to the read. Then I ran the checkpoint's own temp-catalogue walks and both index tests through a probe that loads the checkpoint module. All seven walks came back exactly as the checkpoint expects (`MAIN_PAGES`, `NSFW_PAGES`, the 9-row page then an empty page, 524 sources, 1000 sources, and the unmoderated and moderated walks with identical page-1 cursors), and both index tests passed, under sqlite 3.53.4 in the Engine interpreter. What the tree holds, file by file:\n\n### engine/server/data/random_videos.py\n- `encode_followed_cursor` / `decode_followed_cursor` turn (published_at, video_id, instance_domain) into a base64url JSON cursor and back. Decoding uses `validate=True`, and anything not a string, not base64url or not a 3-item [int, str, str] raises `ValueError(\"Invalid cursor\")`.\n- `fetch_followed_page(conn, channels, accounts, cursor, limit, error_threshold, include_nsfw)` builds one `UNION ALL` term per source (channel by `instance_domain`+`channel_id`, account by `account_url`).\n  - Each term drives from `videos` with a `CROSS JOIN video_embeddings` so it seeks its recency index, and takes at most `limit` rows.\n  - Filters: the shared listing conditions plus dated and not future.\n  - The strict cursor bound is a two-column range plus a three-column tie-break.\n  - Statements are batched at `FOLLOWED_TERMS_PER_STATEMENT = 500` (SQLite's compound-select cap). Each batch takes `2 * limit` rows, the batches are merged in Python in the same DESC order and deduplicated on (video_id, instance_domain).\n  - A cursor is returned only when the page is full.\n\n### engine/server/data/videos.py\n- `ensure_video_indexes` also creates `idx_videos_channel_published ON videos (instance_domain, channel_id, published_at DESC, video_id DESC)` and `idx_videos_account_published ON videos (account_url, published_at DESC, video_id DESC)`, both `IF NOT EXISTS`, and the docstring now says so.\n\n### engine/server/db/jobs/sync-whitelist.py\n- The content schema script creates the same two indexes with `IF NOT EXISTS`, next to `idx_videos_published`.\n\n### engine/server/db/jobs/ensure-video-indexes.py\n- Only the argparse description changed: it now names the per-channel and per-account Following indexes.\n\n### engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py\n- `following` added to `FEED_MODES`.\n- `_parse_follows`: the whole field is refused if any part has the wrong shape.\n- `_handle_similar_request` validates `follows` and `cursor` at the request edge, so bad input gets a 400 rather than reaching `_handle_similar`, where a `ValueError` becomes a 500. Answers: 400 `Invalid follows payload`; 400 `Too many follow sources in request body` when channels plus accounts exceed `MAX_FOLLOW_SOURCES`; 400 `Invalid cursor`. Both values go into the request context.\n- New `_handle_following`: no follows gives an empty page with no cursor. Otherwise it serves `fetch_followed_page` under `db_lock`, then moderation through `_respond_rows`; moderation runs after selection, so it can shorten the page but never moves the cursor.\n- `_respond_rows` gained an optional `cursor` keyword.\n- Dispatch order: `random=1`/`mode=random` first, then `following`, then the ordered feeds. Seeded requests still ignore `mode`.\n\n### engine/server/api/request_context.py\n- `set_request_follows`/`fetch_request_follows` and `set_request_cursor`/`fetch_request_cursor`; `clear_request_context` clears both.\n\n### engine/server/api/server_config.py\n- `MAX_FOLLOW_SOURCES = 1000`, with a `rat-tail:` comment saying it mirrors the Client's `MAX_FOLLOWS`.\n\n### tests/active/test_videos.py\n- The expected index set now includes the two recency indexes.\n\n### tests/active/test_similar.py\n- `following` is listed in `POST_BUILD_MODES`, the modes with no pre-build spelling.\n\n### tests/active/test_random_videos.py, tests/active/test_sync_whitelist.py\n- No edit needed. Neither references the Following read or the new indexes, and nothing in them conflicts with it.\n\n### .scratch/follow-channels-and-accounts/following_query_timing.py\n- The AC8 timing script. It copies the dev `whitelist.db`, times `ensure_video_indexes` on the copy, then times first, next and last pages through `fetch_followed_page` for five fixed sets of followed sources and prints one batch's query plan, along with the sqlite version.\n\n### tests/tmp/probe_following_phase1.py\n- My throwaway probe, now emptied to a single \"delete this file\" comment. I have no tool that deletes files, so it still needs removing.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone. The Step 6 prerequisite is already met: a read-only probe of `engine/server/db/whitelist.db` shows `idx_videos_channel_published` and `idx_videos_account_published` already built with the expected keys, so the conftest Engine's start will not spend its window building them.\n</awaiting_operator>",

A case-sensitive lookup, or one through `videos` (this channel has no video row), answers 404.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_54_follow_channels_and_accounts_phase2.py:242, :244, :245 \u2014 an exact-pair channel miss answers 404 `Channel not found in Engine`, an unknown uuid answers 404 `Video not found in Engine` for both kinds, and nothing is stored</assertion>\n<expected>(404, {\"error\": \"Channel not found in Engine\"}); (404, {\"error\": \"Video not found in Engine\"}) twice; []</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A lookup on channel_id alone finds a channel and stores it (201). Echoed literal: no. Every expected key and label is read from whitelist.db (`_labelled_video`, `_videoless_channel`, the `channels` rows), which is independent of the routes. The test never lowercases or strips the input to build the expected value; the expected value is the catalogue row. These production lines turn the assertions red if deleted:\n- the Engine-row target in `_handle_follow_add` (`follow_target(...)` on the resolved row): :203, :225;\n- the `DELETE FROM blocks` in `add_follow`: :377;\n- the `DELETE FROM follows` in `add_block`: :397;\n- the `raise FollowLimitReached` inside `with conn:` before the writes: :305/:311.\n\n4. One value: yes, fixed. The channel form's stored key was read at one input (:225). I added :298, which checks the stored key set across all 1000 catalogue channels the limit test follows. Labels: channel and account labels are read at different videos and channels (:203, :205, :225). Malformed bodies cover nine shapes, and the 401 test covers three headers on three routes.\n\n5. The double: no. `limited_client` points at CLOSED_ENGINE, an unreachable address, not a stand-in for project code. The three requests it drives (GET list, POST add `{}`, POST remove `{}`) answer before any Engine call. Every other test runs the real Client against the real session Engine, including the real `/internal/channels/resolve` once it exists.\n\n6. It collects: yes. Every name comes from the conftest import line or this module, and `ClientBackend.request(method, path, headers=, body=)` and `.db_path` are used as conftest defines them. The collect-only summary handed to me reads \"no tests\". I have not confirmed why; my guess is that its lane line counts outcomes and a collect-only pass has none. What I do know is that both full runs printed `collected 22 items`, which matches what I wrote: 1+1+1+9 (malformed) +1+1+1+1+3 (429) +3 = 22.\n\n7. Observed, not predicted: partly. These values were observed. A probe (`tests/tmp/probe_54_phase2_premises.py`, now emptied) ran the existing block routes on the same videos through the same Engine metadata path and `block_target`, and printed:\n   - `(201, {'block': {'kind': 'channel', 'instance_domain': 'videos.yeswiki.net', 'channel_id': '1', 'account_url': '', 'label': 'Main root channel'}})`\n   - the account block `label: 'root'`\n   - `(404, {'error': 'Video not found in Engine'})` for NO_SUCH_UUID\n   - `kind must be channel or account` for kind=video and for no kind\n   - `uuid and host must be non-empty strings` for a uuid without a host and for a channel key under kind account\n   - the one `(401, {'error': 'Profile key required'})` for all three headers on all three block routes\n   - `DELETE (204, None)`\n   - limited block routes: GET 200,200,429 and remove `{}` 400,400,429 with `{'error': 'Rate limit exceeded'}`\n   - the catalogue rows `VIDEOLESS 0ch.tv/1 'Main root channel'`, `HELD ELSEWHERE 3`, the twin yt.orokoro.ru/1 and the unrelated www.yiny.org/10\n   - for the limit test's 1000 channels: 0 upper-case hosts, 0 padded fields, 0 blank or long values, and 0 case collisions across the catalogue.\n\n   The probe also showed that the limiter buckets by ip:path whatever the method: a GET then a POST on /api/profile/blocks shared one bucket. The 429 cases are each a separate parametrised test with its own fresh `limited_client`, so this does not touch them.\n\n   These are predicted and cannot be observed until the phase exists, because the routes and `/internal/channels/resolve` are not there: the `{\"follow\": ...}` and `{\"follows\": [...]}` wrappers (mirrored from the observed `{\"block\"}`/`{\"blocks\"}`), the texts `Channel not found in Engine`, `Name a video or a channel, not both`, `instance_domain and channel_id must be non-empty strings` and `Follow limit reached (1000)` (plan \u00a72.6 and AC4), and the channel form's case-insensitive host match (the checkpoint text). What would confirm them: the phase's own run.\n\n8. Red, not green: yes, it fails. `ValidateTests tests/tmp/test_54_follow_channels_and_accounts_phase2.py` exited 1 with \"22 failed\".\n\n9. Red for the right reason: yes. Every failure is the Client answering `(404, {'error': 'Not found'})` to /api/profile/follows, its answer for a path with no route, so the routes are not wired. Per test:\n   - :203 `assert (404, {'error': 'Not found'}) == (201, ('chann...oot channel'))`.\n   - :225: the same. Its control at :219 passed.\n   - :240 `(404, {'error': 'Not found'}) == (404, {'error...d in Engine'})`. Controls :234-:236 passed.\n   - :267 for all nine malformed cases.\n   - :280 `[404, 404, 404, 404, 404] == [201, 201, 201, 201, 201]`.\n   - :294 `(('0ch.tv', '3'), {'error': 'Not found'}) / assert 404 == 201`. Its control :290 passed. Its comment used to say \"control\"; I relabelled it, because it asserts the phase's own add route on the first of the 1000 (AC4), not a premise.\n   - :327 `assert 404 == 201`.\n   - :341 `(404, {'error': 'Not found'}) == (401, ...)`.\n   - :358 `[404, 404, 404] == [200, 200, 429]` and `[400, 400, 429]` \u00d72.\n   - :375, :392 and :413 `assert 404 == 201`. Controls :373 and the blocks at :412 passed.\n\n   No premise control failed. Where a test fails before its C2 assertion (:294, :327, :392), the call that failed is the phase's own add route, which that assertion needs as setup. No form of that setup can run before the phase is built.\n\n10. Observed expected output: yes, each row's `expected` matches what the run showed. Where a value could not be observed, the row says so. The run did not contradict any row: every assertion it reached failed only on the missing route, and the passing controls (:219, :234-:236, :290, :373) confirmed the catalogue premises the rows rest on. One thing for the implementer to note: :225 needs the channel lookup to match the host whatever its case. The Step 3 impact entry called an exact, case-sensitive match right. The checkpoint text asks for the case tolerance, and the probe found no case collisions in `channels`, so lowercasing the host is safe on this catalogue.\n\nRewrites this turn: the controls at :244 and :269 (question 2), the 1000-key assertion at :298 (question 4), and the relabelled comment at :294 (question 9). I ran the test again after the edits: still 22 failed, exit 1, on the lines above. Beyond the files named: `tests/tmp/probe_54_phase2_premises.py`, my throwaway probe. I have no delete tool, so I emptied it to one comment line, and it should be deleted.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:2": "<changes>\n### client/backend/lib/follows.py (new)\n- Mirrors `blocks.py`. It holds `MAX_FOLLOWS = 1000`, `FollowLimitReached`, `add_follow`, `remove_follow` and `list_follows`, and reuses `blocks._key` for the four key columns.\n- `add_follow` runs in one `with conn:`, in this order: the five-column exists check (a re-follow is a no-op and returns), the count check that raises `FollowLimitReached`, the `INSERT`, then `DELETE FROM blocks` on exactly the same kind and key.\n- A refused follow writes nothing, so the block on its key stays.\n- No `follow_target` alias: the server calls `block_target` directly, so the key and label come from the Engine row in one place.\n- `load_follow_keys` is not written. Only Phase 3's gateway injection needs it.\n\n### client/backend/lib/blocks.py\n- `add_block` deletes the follow on exactly the same kind and key, inside its existing transaction, after the insert. The limit check comes earlier, so `BlockLimitReached` leaves the follow alone.\n- The module and function docstrings now say a block replaces a follow on the same key.\n\n### client/backend/lib/users_store.py\n- A `follows` table beside `blocks`, with the same columns, the same `CHECK` and the same primary key. Docstring updated.\n\n### client/backend/lib/profiles.py\n- `delete_profile` also deletes the profile's `follows` rows, in the same transaction.\n\n### client/backend/lib/engine_api_client.py\n- New `resolve_channel(engine_base_url, instance_domain, channel_id)`, shaped like `resolve_video_seed`. It POSTs `/internal/channels/resolve` through `_post_json`, so the bridge headers go with it.\n- A 404 returns None. Any other non-200 raises `EngineApiError`, and so does a missing or non-dict `channel`.\n\n### client/backend/server.py\n- **Routes:** `GET /api/profile/follows` lists `{\"follows\": [...]}`. `POST /api/profile/follows` and `POST /api/profile/follows/remove` are wired exactly like the block routes: the same `_rate_limit_check` (429), and `_require_profile` (one 401) inside each handler.\n- **Shared lookup:** the uuid/host validation and the Engine lookup (`resolve_video_seed`, then `fetch_metadata_for_entries`, 404 `Video not found in Engine`) moved out of `_handle_block_add` into `_video_row_for_body`, which block add and follow add both call. Block add behaves as before.\n- **`_handle_follow_add`:**\n  - The body goes through `_read_block_body` (400 `kind must be channel or account`).\n  - A body naming both a video and a channel answers 400 `Name a video or a channel, not both`.\n  - **Channel form** (`kind=channel` with `instance_domain`/`channel_id`): both must be non-empty strings of at most 200 characters, or it answers 400 `instance_domain and channel_id must be non-empty strings`. They are stripped, then `resolve_channel` is called. 404 `Channel not found in Engine` when the catalogue lacks the pair. The target is `block_target(\"channel\", engine_row)`.\n  - **Video form**, which every other body takes, so a channel key under kind account or a uuid with no host gets 400 `uuid and host must be non-empty strings`: the target is `block_target(kind, metadata_row)`.\n  - Then `add_follow`: 400 `Follow limit reached (1000)`, or 201 `{\"follow\": target}`.\n  - Engine failures go to `_respond_engine_failure(\"lookup\", \u2026)`.\n- **`_handle_follow_remove`:** a copy of `_handle_block_remove` that calls `remove_follow` and answers 204.\n\n### engine/server/data/channels.py\n- New `fetch_channel(conn, instance_domain, channel_id)`. It does an exact primary-key lookup on `channels` and returns `channel_id`, `instance_domain`, `channel_name` and `display_name AS channel_display_name`. Those are the metadata row's key names, so `block_target`'s label fallback applies unchanged.\n\n### engine/server/api/handlers/internal_client_reads.py\n- New `handle_internal_channel_resolve`. A bad JSON body answers 400 with the reader's error. A missing or blank field answers 400 `Missing instance_domain or channel_id`.\n- It lowercases the stripped host and runs `fetch_channel` under `db_lock`. 404 `Channel not found`, or 200 `{\"ok\": true, \"channel\": {...}}`.\n- Why lower rather than `COLLATE NOCASE`: I checked the dev `whitelist.db`. Every `channels.instance_domain` is lowercase and the PK is `(channel_id, instance_domain)`. Its query plan shows a NOCASE match seeks on `channel_id` alone. That is a scan of every host's channel \"1\", for example.\n- Module docstring updated.\n\n### engine/server/api/router.py\n- `\"/internal/channels/resolve\"` is added to `POST_ROUTES` and to the import, plus a `[bridge gate]` line in the docstring. The existing `/internal/` prefix check gates the route with no extra code.\n\n### engine/server/api/handlers/__init__.py\n- The `internal_client_reads` line names the channel lookup.\n\n### Not changed (from this phase's files list)\n- `engine/server/api/handlers/video.py`: I did not add `channelId`, because the checkpoint does not exercise it. The plan needs it for the video page's initial \"Unfollow channel\" label (AC10). Phase 4's files list does not include `video.py` or `tests/active/test_video.py`, so this has to be added there or in its own step.\n- `tests/active/test_follows.py`, `test_profiles.py`, `test_internal_client_reads.py`, `test_router.py`, `test_engine_api_client.py`, `test_video.py`: not created or edited. See inner_tests.\n- No missing-`channels`-table guard in the Engine lookup. Every metadata read already `LEFT JOIN`s `channels`, so an Engine without that table cannot serve the follow flow in any case.\n\n### What I checked\n- I ran a throwaway probe against the real session Engine and Client: video-form channel and account follows, a block and a follow on the same key replacing each other, an upper-case padded channel form, a 200-character missing id, a both-forms body, and remove.\n- The answers matched the checkpoint's expectations. Each key and label came from the Engine, and the stored host was lowercase.\n- The probe file `tests/tmp/probe_phase2_channels.py` is emptied to one comment line and should be deleted. I have no tool that deletes files.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone. The checkpoint drives the real Client against the real Engine, so the bridge-gated `/internal/channels/resolve` round trip, its 200 and its 404 are all under the gate. Two behaviours are not: the Engine handler's 400 for a missing field (the Client validates before it calls) and `resolve_channel`'s raise on a non-200 or non-404 status. Both are copies of the shape `handle_internal_video_resolve` and `resolve_video_seed` already have, and I did not write tests for them.\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\ntests/tmp/probe_phase2_channels.py - a throwaway probe of the dev catalogue's `channels` schema and host case, and of the follow routes against the session Engine. I emptied it to one comment line because I have no tool that deletes files; it should be deleted.\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",
    "author:tests/tmp/test_54_follow_channels_and_accounts_phase3.py": "<assertions>\ntests/tmp/test_54_follow_channels_and_accounts_phase3.py:176: for a keyed profile with follows, a like, a dislike with centroids, a channel block and an account block, the Engine body's `follows` holds exactly the stored pairs (f1.example,7),(f2.example,7) and the accounts alice and bob. This rules out: no injection; reading blocks instead of follows; leaking the bystander's follow; reversed (channel_id, host) pairs; duplicate entries. Expected follows are what the fixture stored with add_follow; the test does not rebuild them through production's query. Deleting the gateway's follows injection turns 176/188/298 red. Deleting the following branch's limit and over-fetch change turns 180 red. Deleting its no-trim change turns 201 red.\n4. One value: no. The limit is checked at two inputs: 3 on the stub, and 5 against the real Engine at 298, where a doubled 10 would give ten rows from a 12-video channel. Follows are checked at two profiles with different shapes: two channels and two accounts, and a lone account. The cursor is checked with the stub's value and with the real Engine's. Line 298 compares the gateway's page with the Engine's direct answer, which is the claim itself (\"the Engine's own answer to that follow\"). The second page's order is checked against whitelist.db's published_at, a separate source.\n5. The double: no in-process double. The stand-in replaces the project's Engine only at its HTTP boundary. What is being observed is the gateway's outbound request, and recording that request is the only way to see it. The real Engine behind the real gateway carries C1 and C2 again at 298\u2013305.\n6. It collects: yes. The collect-only summary printed \"no tests\", which is that runner's summary line in collect mode. The real run printed `collected 24 items`, which matches what was written: 1+1+1+1 + 2 follows + 8 malformed + 2 URL-safe + 7 other reads + 1 walk = 24. Every import resolved and every fixture bound; the conftest imports and lib helpers ran in the fixture.\n7. Observed: one yes, now rewritten. Line 298 got `[] != [('baccea4d-0699-4521-9344-b7a4699d75f5', '810video.com'), \u2026]`, with no follows reaching the real Engine. The controls passed before each of these: status 200 with one Engine call at 173/185/198, the follow stored (290) and the direct Engine paging the channel (294). The 10 passes are regression guards that already hold: keyless, refused follows, and the seven other reads with limit 6 and rows c0\u2013c2.\n10. Row 199 says plainly that it already passes today.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:3": "<changes>\n### `client/backend/server.py`\n- New `FEED_CURSOR_PATTERN` (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,1024}`). `cursor` is now an allowed body field on `/recommendations` only; `/videos/similar` is unchanged. A `cursor` key whose value is not a string fully matching the pattern answers 400 `Invalid cursor payload` before the Engine is called. That includes `\"cursor\": null`, which would otherwise reach the Engine's own 400. A valid cursor is forwarded unchanged. A browser `follows` field is still refused by the existing body-key allowlist with 400 `Unknown body field: follows`.\n- New module function `_is_following_read(path, query)`. It is true only for `/recommendations` with `mode=following`, no `id` and no `random` other than `0`. That copies the Engine's own rules: it ignores `mode` on a seeded read and serves `random` ahead of following. The decision comes from the query, never from the body's `mode`.\n- `_profile_filter`: on a Following read it still sets the query `limit` to the page size, then sets `page_size` to None. That skips the over-fetch (no `limit` \u00d72) and the trim in `_filter_payload`, so blocked and disliked rows are still dropped but the page is not cut and the Engine's cursor stays in the payload. Keyless and filter-less profiles pass through untouched, as before.\n- `_handle_engine_read_proxy_post`: on a keyed Following read it removes the browser's `likes` and `exclude`, sends no `dislike_centroids`, and adds `follows` built from the existing `list_follows`: `{\"channels\": [[instance_domain, channel_id], ...], \"accounts\": [account_url, ...]}`. Like the stored likes, these are added after sanitising so the browser cannot supply them. Every other keyed read keeps the old stored-likes and centroids replacement unchanged.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",
    "author:tests/tmp/test_54_follow_channels_and_accounts_phase4.py": "<items>\n<item id=\"D25b\">\n<disposition>fixed</disposition>\n<what>The keyless video-page test now runs a second, fresh page whose only step is the \"Follow account\" click (:645). Two assertions carry the clause. :656 is a control: NEEDS_PROFILE_VIDEO_PAGE is absent from both pages' text at load. :658 asserts that on the fresh page the account click was dispatched and the message then appears in the page text. No channel click came before it, and :656 shows the message was not there at load, so an account handler that shows nothing (or only re-enables the button) now fails at :658. Before, the old membership check passed on the message left behind by the step-0 channel click. :659 still checks that the main run's account click was dispatched and that its labels are unchanged. :660 checks the fresh page's labels are unchanged too. :661 checks that neither run sends anything to the follow routes.</what>\n</item>\n</items>\n\n<findings_addressed>\nNeither auditor raised a CRITICAL. I took claim recommendation 1 (D25b): the account message is now asserted on a fresh page that has only the account click (:658), behind a control showing the message is absent at load (:656). I left claim recommendations 2\u20134 alone (the video-page lookup that ignores the host, refused toggles on every surface, the search-page surface): they are not on the ledger and do not block. The shape audit made no recommendations.\n</findings_addressed>\n\n<rows>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_54_follow_channels_and_accounts_phase4.py:389, :391, :393, :395 \u2014 whole-result equality on rows, exhausted and asked for each next() over a full page with cursor c1, an empty page with cursor c2, a short page with cursor c3, then a page with no cursor</assertion>\n<expected>First call: rows [a1,a2,a3], exhausted False, asked [None]. One that swallows the error resolves instead of rejecting at :413.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_54_follow_channels_and_accounts_phase4.py:592, :593 \u2014 home page, keyed, ?mode=following: feed requests are exactly [(\"following\", None), (\"following\", \"c1\")] and the cards shown are [K1, K2]</assertion>\n<expected>Two feed requests, the second carrying cursor c1, and the two rows rendered.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>createFeedPager stops at the empty first page: one request and no cards. A channel lookup by channel_id alone also marks K4 \"Unfollow channel\".</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_54_follow_channels_and_accounts_phase4.py:534, :541, :547, :549 \u2014 home labels after the unfollow and after the follow, unchanged after a refused follow, with card uids identical throughout</assertion>\n<expected>After the unfollow, K1 and K2 read Follow channel. After the follow, K1 and K2 read Unfollow account. K4 never changes. Every docstring bullet has assertions, in this order: pager walk, null-cursor end, error keeps the cursor, keyed Following walk, follows.ts round-trip, follows.ts 401s, keyed/keyless home, keyless Following mode, keyed/keyless video page, keyed/keyless channels page. The follows.ts assertions are tagged C2 because they cover the list the labels come from.\n2. Absence only: no. Every absence has a positive control. \"Nothing sent\" in the keyless tests comes with `dispatched` plus the profile message (and the block wording control). \"No feed request\" in keyless Following mode is controlled by the ?mode=trending run requesting its feed. \"No fetch after exhausted\" rests on the `asked` list, and the scripted 5th/3rd fetch would show \"not scripted\". \"uids unchanged\" is checked next to labels that did change.\n3. Echoed literal: no. Expected values are fixed literals or whitelist.db reads via identity_of. The test never performs production's transformation. Deleting createCursorPager's loop-on-empty-with-cursor turns :391 red, and deleting the list lookup in the card labelling turns :527 red.\n4. One value: no. The pager runs three scripts. Labels are read on several cards and rows in different follow states, including a same-channel_id other-host card and row, and across several toggles.\n5. The double: no owned module is doubled. fetch is stubbed for the page modules because the Client sits behind HTTP. The DOM is a browser stand-in. follows.ts runs against the real Client and Engine. The pager's fetchPage is the injected parameter it is built to take.\n6. It collects: yes. The run collected 14 items (3 pager, 1 + 2 parametrised follows.ts, 4 home, 2 video, 2 channels), matching the test count. (The `--collect-only` table's \"no tests\" is that runner's display; the real run printed \"collected 14 items\".)\n7. Observed, not predicted: in a probe (since emptied) I drove the real Client: search q=music gives a second row on another channel and account; video-form channel and account follows and the channel-form follow return 201 with the key fields as expected; the list returns 3; remove returns 204; relist returns 2; and all eight unknown-key and no-key requests answer 401 {\"error\": \"Profile key required\"}. A second probe confirmed the keyed video page posts /api/profile/blocks on Block channel. The page-harness controls (cards render, \".card-action-status\" carries the keyless block wording, ?mode=trending requests its feed, channels rows render) were observed passing in the run. The labels and texts for the new controls are the phase's own wording from the plan (AC11), not the output of existing code.\nRewrite made in this round (in response to 8/9 below): the first run had the three pager tests failing on their CONTROL (`_pager` line 370, `assert len(results) == calls and \"setup\" not in results[0]`, on `[{'setup': 'TypeError: m.createCursorPager is not a function'}]`). The three follows.ts tests ERRORED at setup (`follows_runner` line 422 \u2192 `_esbuild` line 291, `Could not resolve \".../src/data/follows.ts\"`), so nothing was measured. Fixes: PAGER_RUNNER now builds the pager inside each call's try, so every call yields a result carrying the error, and the control checks only that every next() settled. `_esbuild` gained `check=False` returning success, and `follows_runner` falls back to a profile.ts-only bundle when follows.ts does not build, so each call rejects with \"m.<name> is not a function\" and the C2 assertions read it. Both probes were emptied.\n8. Red, not green: yes. The re-run gave `[exit status 1]` with \"14 failed\".\n9. Red for the right reason: yes. Every failure is now on a judging assertion, with every control passing. Pager: :389, :402, :411 on `{'error': 'm.createCursorPager is not a function', 'exhausted': None, 'asked': []}`. follows.ts: :460 on `{'error': 'm.followVideoSource is not a function'}`, and :477 (both params) on `[{'error': 'm.listFollows is not a function'}, ...]`. Home keyed: :527 with every card `{'channel': [], 'account': []}`. Home keyless: :562, `assert False` over the same empty labels. Keyless Following: :581 on `[{'method': 'POST', 'path': '/recommendations', 'query': {'mode': 'recommendations'}, ...}]`. Keyed Following: :592 on `[('recommendations', None)] == [('following', None), ('following', 'c1')]`. Video keyed: :625, and video keyless: :649, both `([], [])`. Channels keyed: :696, and channels keyless: :718, both reading `'follow': []` per row. Each of these is the missing phase: no createCursorPager, no follows.ts, no follow buttons, no following-mode routing.\n10. Observed expected output: the `expected` columns hold the right-implementation values. Every Client-side shape in them (follow bodies, list contents, the 204, the 401 message) matches what the probe showed. The run contradicted no row: the current values it printed are recorded in each row's wrong_implementation column as what the code reads today.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:4": "<changes>\n### client/frontend/src/data/follows.ts (new)\n- Modelled on `blocks.ts`. `listFollows`, `followVideoSource` (POST `{kind, uuid, host}`), `followChannel` (POST `{kind: \"channel\", instance_domain, channel_id}`) and `unfollow` (POST the four key fields to `/remove`, resolves void). They share one `request()`, whose fallback message is `Follow request failed (n)`. A 401 throws the Client's own `Profile key required`.\n- Lookup helpers: `followLookup(follows = [])`, `isFollowed`, `setFollowed` and `toggleVideoSourceFollow`. A channel's key is `instance_domain::channel_id`; an account's is its URL. A source with no identity is never followed.\n- `toggleVideoSourceFollow` sends the remove with the other kind's fields empty. On a follow it records the key the Client returned.\n- `followLabel` lives in `video-card.ts`, not here. Importing it from here would pull `api-base.ts` (`window.location` at load) into `video-card.ts`, and that would break `test_frontend_video_card.py`'s window-less harness.\n\n### client/frontend/src/data/videos.ts\n- New `createCursorPager(fetchPage)`. It keeps the latest cursor. One `next()` keeps fetching through empty pages until a page has rows or comes back with no cursor, and only the no-cursor page sets `exhausted`. A throw happens before the cursor is reassigned, so the next call asks for the same page.\n- A `rat-tail:` pause of 3 s after every 4 fetches inside one `next()` keeps a long empty walk under the Client's 90 requests a minute.\n- `fetchSimilarVideosPayload` takes an optional 4th argument, `cursor`, and puts it in the body only when set. Existing callers are unchanged.\n\n### client/frontend/src/types/videos.ts\n- `VideosPayload.cursor?: string | null`.\n\n### client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts\n- `\"following\"` added to `FEED_MODES`.\n\n### client/frontend/src/components/video-card.ts\n- `VideoCardOptions.follow?: CardFollow` (`{channel, account}`), and the `actions` comment now names the follow buttons.\n- Action cards gain `data-card-action=\"follow-channel\"` and `\"follow-account\"` buttons after Block account.\n- New exports:\n  - `followLabel(kind, followed)`: \"Follow channel\", \"Unfollow account\" and so on.\n  - `refreshFollowButtons(container, rowForKey, followState)`: relabels the follow buttons in place, so no card is redrawn and its status line stays.\n\n### client/frontend/src/pages/videos/index.ts (home)\n- `followingFeed = !useSimilar && mode === \"following\"`. Without a key, `loadVideos` shows \"Following needs a profile. Create one from the Profile button.\" and sends no request. With a key it uses `createCursorPager(fetchFollowingPage)`, which sends the feed params and the cursor and no exclude.\n- With a key, `listFollows` runs once at module start without holding up the feed. On success it fills `followState` and calls `refreshFollowButtons`; on failure it `console.warn`s.\n- `renderFeedCard` passes `follow: cardFollowState(row)`. `rowForKey` is now one helper, also used by the click handler.\n- `runCardAction`:\n  - The keyless text gets a \"Following\" variant.\n  - A new `follow-*` branch toggles, relabels every card of that source and says `Following <label>.` or `Unfollowed this <kind>.`. It never dislikes and never removes rows.\n  - The block branch calls `setFollowed(..., false)` and relabels right after the block succeeds.\n\n### client/frontend/src/pages/search/index.ts\n- The same follow-list load, `follow:` card option, `rowForKey` and `cardFollowState` helpers, keyless \"Following\" text, `follow-*` branch, and block-clears-follow as home, over `state.rows` and `#search-results`. The docstrings name the follow buttons.\n- The checkpoint does not cover search. I wired it because the shared card now renders follow buttons on every action card, and search cards would otherwise carry dead buttons (AC10 also names search).\n\n### client/frontend/src/pages/video-page/index.ts\n- `VideoMetadata.channelId`, mapped from `/api/video`'s `channelId`. The instance fallback leaves it unset.\n- A module-level `followSource` and `followState`, and a `followsLoaded` promise. That promise is one `listFollows` with a key and an empty lookup without one; a failed fetch `console.warn`s and reads as empty.\n- `enableFollowButtons(uuid, host, metadata)` is called beside `enableBlockButtons`. It fills `followSource`, waits for the list, labels both buttons, then wires and enables them, with the same `dataset.wired` guard as the block buttons.\n- A click:\n  - without a key, shows \"Following needs a profile. Create one from the Profile button on the home page.\" in `#block-status`;\n  - otherwise disables the button and runs `toggleVideoSourceFollow` with the video form;\n  - after a follow, copies the Engine's key into `followSource`;\n  - relabels and shows the result or the error, then re-enables the button.\n- A successful block calls `setFollowed(followState, kind, block, false)` and relabels before it dislikes.\n\n### client/frontend/src/pages/channels/index.ts\n- Each row gets a last cell: a `ghost-button` carrying `data-instance-domain`/`data-channel-id`, labelled \"Follow\"/\"Unfollow\" from the lookup, plus a `.follow-status` span.\n- One delegated click listener on `#channels-body` calls `toggleChannelFollow`:\n  - without a key, it shows the profile-needed text in the row;\n  - otherwise it disables the button and calls `unfollow` (channel key, `account_url: \"\"`) or `followChannel`;\n  - on success it updates the lookup and flips the label; a failure shows the error in the row;\n  - it re-enables the button.\n- With a key, `listFollows` runs once at start. If the rows are already shown and no load is running, the table is redrawn.\n- All three `colspan=\"6\"` are now `colspan=\"7\"`.\n\n### client/frontend/index.html, client/frontend/videos.html\n- A \"Following\" `data-feed-mode=\"following\"` button after Popular.\n\n### client/frontend/video-page.html\n- Disabled `#follow-channel` \"Follow channel\" and `#follow-account` \"Follow account\" buttons in `.block-actions`, after the block buttons.\n\n### client/frontend/channels.html\n- A `<th scope=\"col\">Follow</th>` header cell.\n\n### tests/check-frontend-client-gateway.sh\n- `/internal/channels/resolve` added to the forbidden internal-route pattern.\n\n### tests/active/test_frontend_channels_page.py\n- The stub element gains a no-op `addEventListener() {}`, which the new delegated listener needs (as the draft planned). The \"Plan 54 delivered\" comment covers the store and routes, the Engine read and its two indexes, the gateway's cursor passthrough and the frontend controls. Its \"Still open\" list matches the Step 8 `needs_fresh_red`: the Recommendations layer, the end note and empty states, the Profile modal list, `channelId` on `/api/video`, and reloading the follow list after a key change. The plan it cites, `docs/project/plans/54-follow-channels-and-accounts.md`, exists.</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/roadmap.md\" update=\"no\">Already updated in the diff (22666-22685). Implementation-order step 2 reads PARTIAL **Follow** and lists what was delivered: the store and routes, the controls on cards, the video page and the channels page, and the cursor-paged Following mode over two recency indexes. It also lists what remains: the Recommendations layer, the Profile modal list, and the end note and empty states. F3-M4 lists follows among the per-profile stores. Both agree with what landed.</doc>\n<doc path=\"client/README.md\" update=\"no\">Matches server.py as delivered. It covers the three `/api/profile/follows*` routes with both add forms and their errors: 404 `Channel not found in Engine`, 400 `Name a video or a channel, not both`, 400 `Follow limit reached (1000)`, and a re-follow changing nothing. It also covers 201 `{follow}`, the follow/block swap with the account-over-channel-block exception, delete removing follows, and the single-401 list. On the gateway side it covers Following's no-over-fetch/no-trim rule, follows injected in place of likes and centroids, the browser's likes and exclude dropped, `Unknown body field: follows`, and `cursor` on `/recommendations` only with 400 `Invalid cursor payload` and its pattern. It lists `/internal/channels/resolve`.</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/README.md\" update=\"no\">Already accurate (diff 22686-22725+). The intro says whitelist.db is written to create missing indexes at start. It has a `/internal/channels/resolve` entry with the exact 400/404/200 answers and the lowercased host. The Notes cover the `ensure_video_indexes` build at start. The `mode` note gains `following` in the allowed list, the random precedence, the follows body shape, the cursor semantics, no fallback on an empty set, and moderation never moving the cursor. The NSFW note lists following, and the request-scoped inputs list follows and the cursor. All of it matches similar.py, random_videos.py and internal_client_reads.py as built.</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/OVERVIEW.md\" update=\"no\">Already matches the delivered read (diff 23002-23070). It says six kinds of page and has a Following section. That section covers the sort order, the undated and future-dated exclusion, the per-source `UNION ALL` terms seeking the two indexes, the 500-term `FOLLOWED_TERMS_PER_STATEMENT` batching with the Python merge and de-duplication, a base64url cursor issued only on a full page, the empty page with no fallback, and moderation outside `db_lock`. It says Following ignores `exclude`, that only Following's answer carries `cursor`, that the gateway does no over-fetch or trim in Following, and that `createCursorPager` walks empty pages with a 3 s pause after every 4 fetches, keeping the cursor when a fetch fails.</doc>\n<doc path=\"client/frontend/README.md\" update=\"no\">Already describes the shipped frontend, gaps included (diff 9136-9159):\n- six modes, with the keyless Following message and an empty Following feed reading \"No videos found.\";\n- cursor paging through `createCursorPager`;\n- the card follow buttons and their keyless text;\n- `follows.ts`, with one list load per page, labels refreshing only on the next page load after a key change, and a failed load only `console.warn`ed;\n- the video-page buttons, with the stated `channelId` gap;\n- the channels-page Follow column.\nvideo.py was not changed and no Profile modal list was built, so each of these sentences holds.</doc>\n<doc path=\"DEPLOYMENT.md\" update=\"no\">Already updated (diff 8616-8648). It covers:\n- the start-time index build before `/api/health` answers, which holds the write lock, has no measured time or size, and has an `ensure-video-indexes.py` pre-build command and a disk-sizing note;\n- `/api/profile/follows*` in the 401 route list;\n- the Following exception to over-fetch and trim, with short or empty pages that still carry a cursor;\n- the follows store, the 1,000 cap and the follow/block swap;\n- follows in place of likes and taste vectors;\n- `/internal/channels/resolve` in the boundary contract.</doc>\n<doc path=\"DATA_BUILD.md\" update=\"no\">The paragraph added after the schema checks names both recency indexes with their exact columns. It says the sync job creates them if missing, that every Engine start creates them through `ensure_video_indexes`, and that their first-build time and size are unmeasured, which is still true because the AC8 script was never run. It points to DEPLOYMENT.md for pre-building them. The delivered sync-whitelist.py and videos.py both create the indexes with `IF NOT EXISTS`.</doc>\n<doc path=\"README.md\" update=\"no\">Already updated (diff 8652-8673). It says six home feed modes and describes Following as needing a profile and not being shaped by likes. It lists follows in the profile API row and says a keyed Following request carries follows in place of likes and taste vectors. `/internal/channels/resolve` is in the internal contract row. All of this matches what was delivered.</doc>\n<doc path=\"CONTEXT.md\" update=\"no\">The only change the build needed is in: the **Feed mode** entry lists \"... popular or following\". The **Follow** entry also describes the Recommendations follow layer, which has not been delivered yet, and cites a stale \"(issue 39)\". Step 1 settled leaving both as they are for this plan (the requirements say \"`CONTEXT.md` is not changed by this plan\"), so the operator decides when to change them, most naturally with the next plan that delivers the layer.</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/adr/0007-nsfw-filter-default-at-request-edge.md\" update=\"no\">Still holds. `fetch_followed_page` lives in `data/random_videos.py`, which the ADR's module list already names. It defaults `include_nsfw=True`, and `_handle_following` passes `fetch_request_include_nsfw()`, so the decision is made at the request edge as the ADR requires. `/internal/channels/resolve` is an `/internal/*` lookup, and the ADR's consequences already leave those unfiltered.</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/db/jobs/ensure-video-indexes.py\" update=\"no\">The build already changed the argparse description to name the per-channel and per-account Following indexes (Phase 1), so its one claim about what it builds is accurate.</doc>\n<doc path=\"client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts\" update=\"yes\">Line 10's comment, \"The panel adds language and saved channels here; storage holds this object whole.\", is now false. Saved channels became Follow and are kept per profile in the Client's `users.db`, not in the `feedParams:v1` object; the gateway injects them, never this module. The comment should say only that the panel adds language here. The impact inventory flagged this line as stale, but the checklist did not carry it.</doc>\n<doc path=\"tests/active/conftest.py\" update=\"no\">The `trending_seed` docstring (line 150), \"the shared whitelist.db is never written\", is about that fixture: a private `trending_ranks` file replaces the trending fetch's writes. It is still true of the fixture. The one-time index build at Engine start is a property of Engine start, which DATA_BUILD.md, DEPLOYMENT.md and engine/server/README.md now document.</doc>\n</docs>\n\n<adr_conflicts>\nnone\n</adr_conflicts>",
    "step_9_i2_update:client/README.md": "<changes>\nI updated `client/README.md` for the follow routes, the gateway's Following mode and the channel resolve. I checked each claim against `client/backend/server.py` and `client/backend/lib/follows.py`.\n\n- **Profile delete:** the line now lists follows among the things removed.\n- **Three follow routes, added after the block routes:**\n  - `GET /api/profile/follows` returns `{follows}`, newest first.\n  - `POST /api/profile/follows` takes either the video body or the channel body. The channel body must be confirmed by `/internal/channels/resolve`, and a channel the catalogue lacks gets 404 `Channel not found in Engine`. The route documents 400 `Name a video or a channel, not both`, 400 `Follow limit reached (1000)`, that a repeat follow changes nothing, and 201 `{follow}`. It also says a follow and a block on the same key replace each other, and that an account follow leaves a block on one of its channels in place.\n  - `POST /api/profile/follows/remove` answers 204.\n- **Single-401 list:** the follow routes now appear beside the block routes.\n- **Over-fetch sentences:** \"pages stay full\" now points to Following as the exception, and the mode bullet says the over-fetch applies in every mode except Following.\n- **Stored likes and taste vectors:** this bullet now covers keyed feed requests other than Following.\n- **New Following bullet:** it covers:\n  - the read rule (no `id`, no `random` other than 0);\n  - the injected `follows` shape;\n  - that the gateway drops `likes` and `exclude` and sends no taste vectors;\n  - 400 `Unknown body field: follows` for a follows field sent by the browser;\n  - that a keyless request gets an empty page;\n  - `cursor` on `/recommendations` only, with 400 `Invalid cursor payload` for anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,1024}`;\n  - no over-fetch and no trim, with the cursor passed back unchanged, so pages can be short or empty and still carry a cursor.\n- **Boundary Contract:** `/internal/channels/resolve` is added to the list of Engine internal routes the Client calls.\n- **The 502 line:** I left it unchanged. The channel resolve's failures go through `_respond_engine_failure(\"lookup\", \u2026)` and answer `Engine lookup failed`, which that line already covers.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/README.md": "<changes>\nI updated `engine/server/README.md` to cover the Following feed mode, its body checks and cursor paging, the `/internal/channels/resolve` route, and the two indexes the Engine creates at start.\n\n- **Line 3:** the Engine writes `whitelist.db` in two cases: to create missing tables and indexes at start, and for the per-request metadata write-back. The old line said it never wrote the file. That was already wrong before this build (the start already created the moderation, event, trending and channel tables and indexes), and the two new indexes made it more so.\n- **Route list:** a new bullet for `/internal/channels/resolve`. It takes `{instance_domain, channel_id}`, strips both, lowercases the host and looks the pair up exactly under `db_lock` (`fetch_channel`). It answers 400 for a body that is not JSON, 400 `Missing instance_domain or channel_id`, 404 `Channel not found`, or 200 `{\"ok\": true, \"channel\": {...}}` with the four fields it returns.\n- **`mode` note:**\n  - `following` is added to the mode list and to the 400 `allowed` list, in last place as `FEED_MODES` has it.\n  - `random=1` wins over `following` too.\n  - A new passage gives the contract:\n    - the shape of the body's `follows`, and that a followed account covers every channel it owns;\n    - only embedded videos, newest first by (published_at, video_id, instance_domain) DESC, with undated and future-dated ones left out;\n    - the error threshold and moderation apply;\n    - `exclude` is ignored, and paging is by the body's `cursor`, which a full page carries; the next page starts strictly after the last row;\n    - moderation can shorten a page but never moves the cursor;\n    - no follows gives an empty page with no cursor and no fallback;\n    - the three 400s: `Invalid follows payload`, `Too many follow sources in request body` with `max_allowed`/`received` (`MAX_FOLLOW_SOURCES` 1000), and `Invalid cursor`.\n  - The response sentence now says Following answers with an empty `seed`, and that only Following's answer has a `cursor` key.\n  - How the read is built is left to `OVERVIEW.md`, which the existing pointer already names.\n- **NSFW note:** `following` is added to the list of feed modes the filter covers.\n- **Start-up note:** every start runs `ensure_video_indexes`, which creates any missing `videos` indexes, including `idx_videos_channel_published` and `idx_videos_account_published`. On an existing `whitelist.db` the first start builds them before it serves. For building them ahead of time the note points at `DEPLOYMENT.md`.\n- **Request-scoped input note:** follows and the Following cursor are listed with the likes, centroids and exclude as input the request carries, cleared after each request.\n\nI checked each claim against `similar.py` (the body checks, the dispatch order, `_handle_following`), `internal_client_reads.py`, `random_videos.py` and `server.py:363`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/OVERVIEW.md": "<changes>\nI added the Following feed mode to OVERVIEW.md. It now covers six kinds of page, and the Following mode is described from the Engine read through to the frontend's cursor pager.\n\n- **Short version:** the count is six, and a clause says `following` pages by cursor through the newest videos of the followed sources.\n- **Section 1, new Following bullet:**\n  - `fetch_followed_page` reads the body's channels and accounts, and an account covers every channel it owns.\n  - The order is (`published_at`, `video_id`, `instance_domain`) DESC. Undated and future-dated rows are left out. The error threshold and NSFW rows are filtered inside the query.\n  - Each source is one `UNION ALL` term that seeks `idx_videos_channel_published` or `idx_videos_account_published`, with its own `LIMIT`.\n  - A statement holds at most 500 terms (`FOLLOWED_TERMS_PER_STATEMENT`). Larger sets run in batches that are merged in Python and de-duplicated on (`video_id`, `instance_domain`).\n  - A full page carries a base64url cursor of its last row, and the next page starts strictly after it. With no follows the answer is an empty page with no cursor and no fallback.\n  - Moderation runs after selection and outside `db_lock`, so it never moves the cursor.\n  - It points to `engine/server/README.md` for the body contract instead of repeating it.\n- **Likes Source:** a keyed Following request carries the profile's follows instead of likes or taste vectors. This points to `client/README.md`.\n- **Excluded Videos (Paging):** Following does not apply `exclude`; it pages by cursor.\n- **Section 8, the Engine's batch:** Following is listed among the ordered answers and answers with an empty `seed`. Only Following's answer has a `cursor` key, and only on a full page.\n- **Section 8, the gateway:** in Following the gateway neither over-fetches nor trims, so a page can be short, or empty while still carrying the cursor.\n- **Section 8, frontend paging:**\n  - `createFeedPager` serves every feed except Following.\n  - A new Following bullet describes `createCursorPager`: it sends the cursor and no `exclude`, walks through empty pages, pauses 3 s after every 4 requests, and ends only when a page comes back with no cursor.\n  - A failed fetch keeps the cursor, so the next attempt asks for the same page again.\n\nI checked these claims against `random_videos.py` (`fetch_followed_page` and the cursor encode/decode), `similar.py` (`_handle_following`, `seed_payload={}` and the `cursor` keyword) and `videos.ts` (`createCursorPager`).\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:client/frontend/README.md": "<changes>\nI updated `client/frontend/README.md` to cover the Following feed mode, its cursor paging, and the follow controls on cards, the video page and the channels page.\n\nI checked every statement against the source files: `src/data/feed-params.ts`, `src/data/videos.ts`, `src/pages/videos/index.ts`, `src/pages/video-page/index.ts`, `src/pages/channels/index.ts` and `src/components/video-card.ts`. I also confirmed that neither `engine/server/api/handlers/video.py` nor `client/backend` sends a `channelId`.\n\n- **Feed modes (line 10):** there are now six modes, with Following after Popular. Following keeps the Engine's order and is not shuffled. Without a profile key it shows \"Following needs a profile. Create one from the Profile button.\" and sends no request. An empty Following feed reads \"No videos found.\".\n- **Paging (line 14):** Following pages by cursor through `createCursorPager`. Each request sends the last cursor and no exclude list. A short or empty page that carries a cursor does not end the feed. One batch keeps fetching through empty pages and pauses 3 s after every 4 requests, until a page has rows or comes back with no cursor. Only a page with no cursor ends the feed.\n- **Card actions (line 17):** Follow channel and Follow account join the list of card buttons and the list of buttons that need a key. The keyless wording is \"Following needs a profile. Create one from the Profile button.\".\n- **New \"Follow controls\" bullet,** with one sub-bullet for each page:\n  - **Shared behaviour:** the labels and the `/api/profile/follows` routes. For what those routes accept it points to `client/README.md` rather than repeating it. With a key, each page loads the follow list once. A failed load only logs a `console.warn`, and every control then reads Follow. After Create, Use key or Delete profile, the new state shows from the next page load. Each control is disabled while its request runs and shows the result or the error.\n  - **Cards:** a follow or unfollow relabels every loaded card of that source in place. It never dislikes the video or removes a card. A Block clears the follow label on the blocked key.\n  - **Video page:** `#follow-channel` and `#follow-account` stay disabled until the follow list is known. They report in `#block-status` and use the \"\u2026on the home page.\" keyless wording. Because `/api/video` sends no `channelId`, the channel button reads \"Follow channel\" at load even when that channel is followed.\n  - **Channels page:** a Follow column with a Follow/Unfollow button and a `.follow-status` line on each row. It follows channels only.\n\nAs instructed, the README describes neither the Profile modal's Following list nor the end-of-feed or how-to-follow messages, because they were not built.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:DEPLOYMENT.md": "<changes>\nI updated DEPLOYMENT.md for follows, the Following feed's paging, the channel lookup and the two new indexes built when the Engine starts.\n\n- **Section 5, profile route list:** added `/api/profile/follows*`.\n- **Section 5, blocks paragraph:** feeds are fetched at twice the page size and trimmed in every mode except Following. A Following page is filtered without over-fetching or trimming, so it can come back short, or empty but still carrying the Engine's `cursor`. Also added that a profile holds up to 1,000 follows in `users.db`, and that a follow and a block on the same key replace each other. For how the Following mode works, it points to `client/README.md`.\n- **Section 5, likes/dislikes paragraph:** a keyed Following request sends the profile's follows instead of its likes and taste vectors, and disliked rows are removed without over-fetching.\n- **Section 5, boundary contract:** added `/internal/channels/resolve` to the list of Engine internal routes the Client calls.\n- **Section 2, Blue/green deploy:** a new paragraph says that every Engine start runs `ensure_video_indexes` before it listens. That function builds any missing `videos` index, including `idx_videos_channel_published` and `idx_videos_account_published`. On an existing `whitelist.db` the first start builds them before `/api/health` answers, and holds the write lock while it does. Their build time and size are stated as unmeasured on both dev and prod. It gives two options: build them first with the `ensure-video-indexes.py --db \u2026` command (as the service user, with the updater idle), or raise `--timeout`. It also says the two indexes make `whitelist.db` bigger, so backups and disk sizing should allow for them.\n\nI checked these claims against `engine/server/api/server.py:363` (the index build runs before listening), `engine/server/db/jobs/ensure-video-indexes.py` (the `--db` argument), and in `client/backend/server.py` `_profile_filter` and `_handle_engine_read_proxy_post` (no over-fetch or trim, and follows replace likes and taste vectors). I also checked the `/internal/channels/resolve` call in `client/backend/lib/engine_api_client.py`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:DATA_BUILD.md": "<changes>\nDATA_BUILD.md, step 2: added one paragraph on the two Following recency indexes. It says where they are created, that their cost is unmeasured, and points to `DEPLOYMENT.md` for building them ahead of a deploy.\n\n- **Where it goes:** right after the schema-check list in \"2) Filter to JoinPeerTube whitelist\".\n- **What it says:**\n  - `sync-whitelist.py` creates `idx_videos_channel_published (instance_domain, channel_id, published_at DESC, video_id DESC)` and `idx_videos_account_published (account_url, published_at DESC, video_id DESC)` if they are missing. I checked this in `ensure_content_schema`, lines 406-409.\n  - Every Engine start also creates them through `ensure_video_indexes` in `engine/server/data/videos.py`. I checked this at lines 23-26.\n  - Their first-build time and size have not been measured.\n- **Pointer, not a copy:** how to pre-build the indexes, and how the build holds the write lock during deploys, is already in `DEPLOYMENT.md` (line 198). This doc points there instead of repeating it.\n- **Claim left out:** the checklist said \"a full sync or merge maintains them\". I did not write that the updater merge creates them, because I could not confirm the merge runs `ensure_content_schema`.\n- **Section left alone:** the \"Reclaiming freed space\" section is about the indexes that get dropped, and it is still accurate, so I did not change it.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:README.md": "<changes>\nI updated README.md: the home feed modes paragraph now lists six modes, including Following, and the boundary-contract table names follows, the follows sent in place of likes on a Following request, and `/internal/channels/resolve`.\n\n- **Home feed modes (line 45):** \"five\" is now \"six\", with Following listed after Popular. One sentence says Following shows the newest videos of the channels and accounts the profile follows, needs a profile, and is not shaped by likes. The existing pointers to the frontend README, the Engine README and OVERVIEW.md stay as they were and cover the rest, such as cursor paging and the mode parameter.\n- **Write/profile API row (line 51):** follows is added beside blocks.\n- **Read gateway row (line 53):** a keyed Following request carries the profile's follows instead of its likes and taste vectors. I checked this in `_handle_engine_read_proxy_post` in `client/backend/server.py`: on a Following read it removes `likes` and `exclude`, sends no centroids, and adds `follows` built from `list_follows`.\n- **Internal Client->Engine row (line 54):** `/internal/channels/resolve` is added. I checked it in `engine/server/api/router.py` and in `resolve_channel` in `engine_api_client.py`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:CONTEXT.md": "<changes>\nI added `following` to the list of modes in the CONTEXT.md **Feed mode** entry. Please confirm this edit, because Step 1 had decided CONTEXT.md would not change.\n\n- Line 23 now reads: \"recommendations (the default), trending, recent, random, popular or following.\"\n- I checked this against the code. `FEED_MODES` in `engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py:89` and in `client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts:6` both include `following`.\n- The entry already says a feed mode \"applies only to unseeded requests\", and that holds for Following: in `similar.py` (lines 991\u20131002), seeded requests are forced to `recommendations`, and the `following` branch only runs after the random check. So nothing else in the entry needed to change.\n- I did not change the **Follow** entry (line 14), as Step 1 decided. Its stale \"(issue 39)\" is still there, and it still describes the Recommendations follow layer, which does not exist yet.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/issues/59-follow-channels-and-accounts.md": "<changes>\nI updated issue 59. Its status is now `ready-for-agent`, the Q1\u2013Q7 answers are recorded, and a new comment says what plan 54 delivered and what is still open.\n\n- **Status:** `needs-triage` \u2192 `ready-for-agent`. The issue is planned and part-built, and `triage-labels.md` has no separate \"planned\" state, so `ready-for-agent` is its closest label for open work. The issue stays open and has not moved to the archive.\n- **\"Open questions\" is now \"Questions and answers\":**\n  - Q1\u2013Q3, Q5 and Q7 carry the settled answers. I checked them against the code: `MAX_FOLLOWS = 1000` in `follows.py`, the `Follow limit reached` error in `server.py`, and `MAX_FOLLOW_SOURCES = 1000` in `server_config.py`.\n  - Q4 is marked open and deferred to the next plan.\n  - Q6 is answered but marked \"planned, not yet built\".\n  - The section points to `docs/project/plans/54-follow-channels-and-accounts.md`.\n- **Related, roadmap M1 line:** it said the Following mode would inherit the `exclude` paging limit. It now says Following pages by cursor, while trending, recent and popular still use `exclude`.\n- **New comment, \"Plan 54 delivered (2026-10-05)\":**\n  - It says the two dated \"Checked in the tree\" notes (no follow code, no Engine query by source) no longer hold. The dated section itself is unchanged.\n  - It summarises what exists now: the store and routes, the Engine read and its indexes, how the gateway injects follows and passes the cursor through, and the frontend controls and Following mode.\n  - It lists what is still open: the Recommendations layer, the Following end note and empty states, the Profile modal list, `channelId` on `/api/video` (I confirmed `video.py` still doesn't send it), and reloading the follow list after Create, Use key or Delete profile.\n- I left the stale `(issue 39)` note about `CONTEXT.md` as it is; the plan keeps that file unchanged.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",

It points at issue 59 and `docs/project/plans/54-follow-channels-and-accounts.md`.\n  - **Delivered:** per-profile follows of channels and accounts in `users.db`, with their routes. Follow controls on feed and search cards, the video page and the channels page (channel follow only). The Following feed mode, paged by cursor over two per-source recency indexes.\n  - **Detail:** it points at `client/README.md` and `engine/server/README.md` rather than repeating them.\n  - **Remaining:** the Recommendations follow layer (the next plan), the Profile modal's Following list, and the Following end note and empty states. For anything else still open it points to the issue rather than copying the issue's list.\n- **F3-M4 (line 83):** now reads \"Likes, dislikes, blocks and follows are stored per profile in the Client's `users.db`\".     "step_9_i2_update:client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts": "<changes>\nI fixed the stale comment on `FeedParams` in `client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts`: it now says only that the panel adds language here.\n\n- Line 10 now reads `// The panel adds language here; storage holds this object whole.`\n- I took out \"saved channels\". They have become follows, which are stored per profile in the Client's `users.db` and added to the request by the gateway.   "requirements": "### Source and purpose\n\nSource issue: `docs/project/issues/59-follow-channels-and-accounts.md`. It asks for the **Follow** defined in `CONTEXT.md`, which replaces the roadmap's \"saved channels\" (feed panel I4 and I5, `docs/project/plans/archive/04-feed-parameter-panel.md`). A follow is a profile's positive mark on a channel (`instance_domain` + `channel_id`) or an account (`account_url`). It is keyed like a block, and following an account covers every channel the account owns. A follow and a block on the same source replace each other. A follow stays on this site and is never sent over ActivityPub. It is not roadmap F2-M5.\n\nThe operator set two equal goals (2026-10-04), and Follow is useful only with both:\n- **Catch up:** a feed of the newest videos from the channels and accounts the visitor follows. This plan delivers it.\n- **Steer:** the home Recommendations mix leans towards the followed sources. The next plan delivers it, reusing this plan's Engine read.\n\nThe route is **Rt1** (operator, 2026-10-04): a `following` mode on `/recommendations`. The gateway injects the profile's stored follows into the Engine request, and two new per-source indexes on `videos` serve the read. These were rejected: Rt1b (the same mode with no index, measured at 0.8\u20131.4 s warm for quiet sets and for last pages, while holding the shared connection's lock); Rt2 (the gateway builds the feed from a new `/internal/...` read, which would be a second place that builds feeds); Rt3 (follows stored in the Engine, which holds no profile state).\n\n### Scope\n\nIn this plan (54):\n- the per-profile follow store in the Client backend's `users.db`, and its routes;\n- Follow and Unfollow controls on the video page, on home feed and search cards, and on the channels page (channel follow only, because a channels-page row has no `account_url`);\n- a list of the profile's follows, each with an Unfollow button, in the home page's Profile modal;\n- an Engine read of the newest videos from a set of followed sources, with two new indexes;\n- the Following home feed mode, paged by a cursor.\n\nOut of scope:\n- the follow layer in the home Recommendations mix (the next plan). Until it lands, following something changes only the Following mode;\n- sending follows over ActivityPub;\n- follows in up-next or in the global feed modes (Trending, Recent, Random, Popular), which stay untouched;\n- importing follows into a profile;\n- the roadmap's M1 cursor item for the other ordered modes, which keep their `exclude` paging.\n\n`CONTEXT.md` is not changed by this plan. Its Follow definition also describes the Recommendations layer, which arrives in the next plan.\n\n### Acceptance criteria \u2014 store and routes (Client backend)\n\n- **AC1:** a keyed profile can add, list and remove follows.\n  - Each follow is either a channel, keyed `(instance_domain, channel_id)`, or an account, keyed `account_url`, with `''` in the unused columns as `client/backend/lib/blocks.py` does. Each carries a display label.\n  - The key and the label always come from the Engine's record, never from the browser.\n  - The routes mirror the block routes' shape, rate limits and 401 behaviour. The block routes are `GET /api/profile/blocks`, `POST /api/profile/blocks` and `POST /api/profile/blocks/remove` in `client/backend/server.py`. Each is rate-limited and needs `X-Profile-Key` through `_require_profile`, which answers a single 401 for every failure. Removing takes the stored key fields, as block removal does.\n- **AC2:** a follow can be added in two forms.\n  - **From a video:** named by `uuid`, `host` and `kind` (`channel` or `account`), as `_handle_block_add` does. The video is resolved through the Engine, and the target is read from the Engine's metadata row, as `block_target` does.\n  - **For a channel, from `(instance_domain, channel_id)`:** this serves the channels page. The gateway accepts the channel only once the Engine's catalogue confirms it exists, and takes the label from the Engine. It answers 404 when the catalogue does not hold that channel. The operator approved this as a deliberate, bounded exception to the block rule that \"the browser never supplies a channel id\" (2026-10-04): the browser names the channel, and the Engine vouches for it.\n- **AC3:** adding a follow removes a block on the same key, and adding a block removes a follow on the same key. Following an account does not remove a block on one of the account's channels, and the gateway still filters that channel's videos out.\n- **AC4:** limits and lifecycle.\n  - A profile holds at most 1000 follows, channels and accounts together (a `MAX_FOLLOWS`, like `MAX_BLOCKS = 1000`).\n  - Adding a new follow past the limit answers 400 `{\"error\": \"Follow limit reached (1000)\"}`.\n  - Adding a follow already held succeeds without making a duplicate.\n  - Deleting the profile deletes its follows.\n\n### Acceptance criteria \u2014 Following mode (Engine and gateway)\n\n- **AC5:** `mode=following` is accepted on unseeded `/recommendations` requests. It joins the Engine's `FEED_MODES` (`engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py:84`) and the frontend's mirror in `client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts`.\n  - For a keyed profile, the gateway adds the profile's stored follows to the Engine request body. It does so after sanitising, in the same place and way it adds `likes` and `dislike_centroids` (`_handle_engine_read_proxy_post`), so the browser cannot supply them.\n  - A follows field sent by the browser is not in the `/recommendations` body allowlist (`PROXY_ALLOWED_BODY_KEYS`). It is rejected with the existing 400 `Unknown body field: <key>`.\n  - The cursor joins that allowlist and is validated in the gateway.\n  - A keyless request for the mode, or one from a profile that follows nothing, answers an empty page with no cursor and no random or other fallback.\n- **AC6:** the Engine returns the videos from the followed channels and from every channel of the followed accounts, newest first by `(published_at DESC, video_id DESC)`.\n  - Each answer carries an opaque cursor for the next page, or none when nothing is left.\n  - Given that cursor, the next page starts strictly after the last row the Engine returned.\n  - No video repeats and none is skipped across pages as served to the browser, whatever the gateway filters.\n  - **Gateway paging rule (operator-approved, 2026-10-04):** in Following mode the gateway does not over-fetch (`FEED_OVERFETCH_FACTOR`) and does not cut filtered rows to the page size (`_filter_payload`). It removes blocked and disliked rows and passes the Engine's cursor through unchanged. A served page can therefore be short, or empty while still carrying a cursor.\n- **AC7:** the mode applies the same filters as the other ordered feeds: the video error threshold, serving moderation, the NSFW filter (`include_nsfw` passed from the request edge, ADR-0007, `NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL`), and the gateway's blocks and dislikes.\n- **AC8:** with the new indexes, the database read for one page of any followed set of up to 1000 sources takes at most 0.1 s, warm, on the dev `whitelist.db`. This includes the last page and sets of quiet sources.\n  - The operator confirmed the budget (2026-10-04).\n  - The build reruns the five measured sets against the new indexes and records the numbers. The sets are 20 small channels, 5 multi-channel accounts, 20 small channels plus 5 accounts, 5 big channels, and 1000 random channels.
